title: Regularity thresholds for anomalous dissipation and related phenomena in passive scalars
summary: We prove the absence of anomalous dissipation for passive scalars driven by some random autonomous divergence-free vector fields in $\mathbb T^d$. In dimension $d=2$ we just need continuity almost surely and a mild nondegeneracy condition on the randomness. In dimension $d\geq 3$ we assume a special geometric structure and almost sure Hölder regularity with a Hölder exponent bigger than $\frac{1}{8}$. No regularity is assumed on the passive scalar except for boundedness in the initial data. The proof relies on dimension-theoretic arguments, as opposed to commutator estimates. A consequence…
